explain.say: So remember four steps: stop, save it, block and report, and tell a trusted adult like a parent, carer or teacher. Brilliant! Remember: what someone sends you is never your fault.

faq.q: Should I reply to a mean message?
faq.a: No. Replying often makes the bully want to keep going. Stop, take a breath, and save the message instead.
asks: Should I reply to a cyberbully?

faq.q: How do I block and report someone?
faq.a: Most apps have a block button and a report button, often found by tapping the person's name or the three dots. Ask a grown-up to help you if you are not sure.
asks: Tell me about the Block and report

faq.q: Who should I tell about something online?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a grandparent, a teacher or a school counsellor. You will not be in trouble for telling.
asks: Tell me about the Tell a trusted adult

faq.q: Why should I take a screenshot?
faq.a: A screenshot keeps proof of what was said, even if the person deletes it later. It helps adults and schools take action.
asks: Tell me about the Save it

faq.q: What if I see something online that scares me?
faq.a: Close it or turn the screen over, and tell a trusted adult straight away. It is never your fault that you saw it.

facts: Most social media and gaming apps have built-in tools to block and report users who send hurtful messages.
Keeping screenshots of mean messages helps schools and adults take action against cyberbullying.
